## Flores — capital of the island of Petén

The beautiful island capital lies among mountains and lush jungle, where ruins of Maya buildings have survived on the mountaintops. Tikal is a magical place that attracts travelers from many countries. The city is known for its pyramids, temples, observatories, and palaces. Miles of humid forest provide a habitat for a wide variety of animals and birds.

Flores lies in northeastern Guatemala. It is the center of El Petén, the country's largest department, which covers about one-third of Guatemala's territory. Its historic quarter is on an island in Lake Petén Itzá. Jungle-covered land begins not far from the town. There, in Tikal National Park northeast of Flores, stands one of the largest ancient Maya cities.

## Staying in Flores

### Tikal & Flores — ruins in the jungle!

Travelers visiting this remarkable area often enjoy staying in small hotels around the lake. The setting is exceptionally scenic, with sweeping panoramic views of the surroundings. At Tikal, deep in the lush jungle, stands an ancient ceremonial center, one of the most impressive of the Maya world. Vast, sparsely populated tracts covered in rainforest still hold many mysteries, making the area attractive to archaeologists and curious travelers alike.
